known_limitations: The search is systematic and citation-chained but is not a registered systematic review.
Legacy Q1-Q10 are not reproducible saturation evidence; Q11/Q12 are reproducible but superseded by transfer-ladder scope expansion; Q13/Q14 are the latest usable producer-side rounds.
Search interfaces do not expose stable raw database hit counts; fresh rounds freeze the unique primary candidates actually opened and screened.
Several arXiv works may later receive proceedings versions and require a final pre-submission refresh.
AgenticQwen exact per-model size details are not inferred from the abstract; the control table explicitly leaves exact sizes to primary-paper review rather than inventing values.
No producer-side validator or saturation result establishes novelty acceptance, priority wording or GATE-001 PASS.
unexpected_findings: SOP-Agent directly occupies the broad decision-graph/SOP routing mechanism that ENG-200 might otherwise appear to introduce.
PA-Tool makes tool-schema naming a concrete causal alternative: small-model tool-use gains can arise without training or teacher reasoning.
SmartAD, Skill-Aware, REDI and AgenticQwen make the teacher-to-small-model weight-adaptation boundary dense rather than hypothetical.
Distillation-induced tool-use action-graph convergence is measurable and must not be confused with the fixed-weight semantic-placement mechanism.
The independent re-review round-2 scope refresh did not force a PIVOT of the fixed-weight core claim; it forced stricter boundary accounting around ENG-200/201/202.
